text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
English cricketer Dr WILLIAM GILBERT GRACE, who scored almost 55,000 runs and more than 2,800 wickets in his career, was born in 1848.

South Australian saddler and carriage maker, HENRY HOLDEN, was born in 1859. He built Dodge cars after World War One, and his company merged with General Motors. This new company, General Motors Holden, went on to become the most famous in Australian motoring history.
American comic actor RED SKELTON was born in 1913.
American astronaut JOHN GLENN was born in 1921.

United States singer and songwriter DION (DION DI MUCCI) was born in 1939. In 1957 he formed 'Dion and the Timberlanes' and a year later 'Dion and the Belmonts'. His hits included "A Teenager in Love" (1959), "Runaround Sue" (1961), "The Wanderer" (1961) and "Ruby Baby" (1963).
British bass player DANNY McCULLOCH, who played with the 'Savages' and the 'Animals' before going solo, was born in 1945.

Australian fast bowler DENNIS KEITH LILLEE was born in Subiaco in Perth in 1949. He made his first-class cricket debut at the age of 20, and became Test crikcet's top wicket taker, with 310 wickets in 58 tests. LILLEE's final tally in first-class cricket was 845 wickets and more than 2,000 runs. English bowler IAN BOTHAM broke LILLEE's wicket-taking record in 1986.
The "Man in Leather" from the 'Village People' GLENN HUGHES was born in 1950.
American actress AUDREY LANDERS, who was best known as "Afton Cooper" in 'Dallas', was born in 1958.
** EVENTS **
64 : The great fire of Rome destroyed two-thirds of the
city. The emperor NERO suspected Christians of causing it and they were subsequently persecuted.
1814 : Construction began on the road over the Blue
Mountains, west of Sydney. The road running from Emu Plains to Bathurst was competed by January, 1815.
1814 : The book "A Voyage To Terra Australis", written by

explorer MATTHEW FLINDERS, was published in London. The book was credited with bringing the word "Australia" into common use. Prior to that, the country was referred to as "New Holland". The name Australia came from the Latin word "australia" meaning "southern." "Terra Australis" means "southern land".
1817 : English author JANE AUSTEN, whose works included
"Emma", "Pride and Prejudice" and "Sense and Sensibility", died.
1870 : The First Vatican Council declared the Dogma of
Papal Infallibility in matters of faith and morals.
1877 : THOMAS EDISON recorded the human voice for the
first time.
1925 : ADOLF HITLER published "Mein Kampf" (My Struggle).
He wrote the book while imprisoned after the Nazi Party's abortive coup against the Bavarian government.
1928 : Sir JAMES FAIRFAX, part-owner of the Sydney
Morning Herald, died while playing golf.
1936 : General FRANCO's Spanish army rose up against the
Republican government in the early hours of the morning with a revolt at Melilla in Spanish Morocco.
1955 : The fantasy-world creation of film producer WALT
DISNEY, Disneyland, opened in California. The first of the modern amusement parks was divided into four sections, Fantasyland, Frontierland, Adventureland, and Tomorrowland.
1967 : A new inquiry began in Sydney into the 'Voyager'
disaster.
1969 : Senator EDWARD KENNEDY crashed his car off the
Chappaquidick Island bridge; his passenger, MARY JO KOPECHNE, died in the accident.
1971 : Six Trucial States, Abu Dhabi, Dubai, Sharjah, Umm
al-Quwain, Ajman & Fujeirah, decided to form the Union of Arab Emirates.
1976 : RAELENE BOYLE became the first woman to carry the
Australian flag at the opening ceremony of the Olympic Games in Montreal.
1979 : A woman charged in Britain with kidnapping a
Mormon missionary and using him for sexual purposes was arrested in the United States.
1984 : 20 people were killed and 16 others were injured
when a security guard when on a shooting rampage in a McDonald's restaurant in California.
1989 : More than three million dollars worth of ivory was

torched by Kenya's president DANIEL ARAP MOI. The president was demonstrating his personal commitment to saving the elephant, and his campaign against the ivory trade. The 12 tons of stockpiled ivory was destroyed.
1990 : Talks began in Washington between the United
states and Vietnam on the future of Cambodia.
1994 : Brazil won the soccer World Cup in a penalty
shoot-out againt Italy in the United States.
1994 : 96 people were killed when a bomb ripped through a
Buenos Aires Jewish community centre.
